column3: NASB follows the critical text (“the Lamb,” “His name and the name of His Father”).
NASB follows the critical text (“the voice which I heard”); “harping” is rendered “playing on.”
“Are singing as a song” is rendered “sang a new song”; “redeemed” is rendered “purchased.”
NASB follows the critical text; “pure” is rendered “they have kept themselves chaste,” and “redeemed” “purchased.”
NASB follows the critical text (“lie”), without “before the throne of God.”
NASB follows the critical text (“to those who live on the earth”); “glad tidings” is rendered “gospel.”
NASB follows the critical text; “saying” is rendered “he said.”
NASB follows the critical text (“a second one,” “Babylon the great”); “wrath” is rendered “passion,” and “Gentiles” “nations.”
NASB follows the critical text (“another angel, a third one”).
“Anger … wrath” is rendered “wrath … anger,” and “mixed undiluted” “mixed in full strength.”
“To ages of ages” is rendered “forever and ever.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “the faith of Jesus” as “their faith in Jesus.”
NASB follows the critical text, without “to me”; “works” is rendered “deeds.”
NASB follows the critical text; it writes “son of man” in lowercase.
NASB follows the critical text; “put forth” is rendered “Put in,” and “has ripened” “is ripe.”
NASB follows the critical text (“on the cloud”); “harvested” is rendered “reaped.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text (“the one who has power”); “authority” is rendered “power.”
NASB follows the critical text (“great”); NASB supplies “the clusters from.”
“One thousand six hundred stadia” is rendered “two hundred miles.”
